questions.stem: Large homogenous eosinophilic inclusions in plasma cells are called:
questions.solutionHtml:
Russell bodies

The globular inclusions in the plasma cells are referred to as Russell bodies (if cytoplasmic) or Dutcher bodies (if nuclear).



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: The single most important predictor of survival in multiple myeloma:
questions.solutionHtml:
Serum β2 microglobulin
  • Serum β2 -microglobulin is the single most powerful predictor of survival and can substitute for staging.
  • β2-Microglobulin concentration is the strongest and most reliable prognostic factor for multiple myeloma.
  • It depends not only on the tumour burden but also on renal function. Elevated β2-M values predict early death.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 798

questions.stem: False statement about monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance

options.label: D
options.text: Does not progress to multiple myeloma

questions.answerText: Does not progress to multiple myeloma
questions.solutionHtml:
Does not progress to multiple myeloma
  • 1% monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance progresses to multiple myeloma every year.

MGUS (Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance):

  • MGUS is the most common plasma cell disorder
  • No Bence Jones proteinuria seen.
  • No organ impairment.
  • M protein < 3 g/dL
  • Bone marrow plasma cells < 10%
  • Patients are asymptomatic
  • Can progress to Multiple Myeloma.
  • As with smouldering myeloma, progression to multiple myeloma is unpredictable; hence, periodic assessment of serum M component levels and Bence Jones proteinuria is warranted.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: Multiple myeloma is a tumour of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Plasma cell
  • Multiple myeloma is a malignant proliferation of plasma cells derived from a single clone.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: A patient presents with bone pain. X-ray reveals destructive lesions. Lab investigations show hypercalcemia. Serum electrophoresis shows an M spike, while Bone marrow shows 35% plasma cells. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple myeloma
  • In the given scenario, the patient has bone pain, destructive bony lesions on X-Ray, hypercalcemia, M spike and 35% plasma cells in the Bone marrow which is diagnostic of Multiple Myeloma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: Beta-2 –microglobulin is a tumour marker for-
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple myeloma
  • The tumour marker for multiple myeloma is Serum β2 microglobulin
  • Serum β2 microglobulin level < 3.5mg/L indicates a good prognosis

  • Serum β2 microglobulin is the single most powerful predictor of survival and can substitute for staging.
  • β2-Microglobulin concentration is the strongest and most reliable prognostic factor for multiple myeloma.
  • It depends not only on the tumour burden but also on renal function. Elevated β2-M values predict early death.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 336, 607-610

questions.stem: Proliferation and survival of myeloma cells are dependent on which of the following cytokines?
questions.solutionHtml:
IL-6
  • IL-6 helps in the survival and proliferation of myeloma cells.
  • The proliferation and survival of myeloma cells are dependent on several cytokines, most notably IL-6, which is an important growth factor for plasma cells.
  • It is produced by the tumour cells themselves and by resident marrow stromal cells.
  • High serum levels of IL-6 are seen in patients with active disease and are associated with a poor prognosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: For Multiple myeloma, all are true, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Dystrophic calcification

Calcification in multiple myeloma is due to hypercalcemia (metastatic calcification) and not dystrophic calcification.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 65, 66, 607-610

questions.stem: Bence Jones proteinuria is derived from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Light chain globulins
  • The Excretion of light chains in the urine has been referred to as Bence Jones proteinuria.
    Light chains include κ and λ (kappa and lambda)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
  • Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma:
  • Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is a B-cell neoplasm of older adults that usually presents in the sixth or seventh decade of life.
  • Although superficially resembling CLL/SLL, it differs in that a substantial fraction of the tumour cells undergo terminal differentiation to plasma cells.
  • Most commonly, the plasma cell component secretes monoclonal IgM, often in amounts sufficient to cause a hyperviscosity syndrome known as Waldenström macroglobulinemia.
  • Unlike multiple myeloma, complications stemming from the secretion of free light chains (e.g. Renal failure and amyloidosis) are relatively rare, and bone destruction does NOT occur.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 601, 610, 611

questions.stem: The Russel body is seen in -
questions.solutionHtml:
Plasma cells
  • Russel bodies are seen in Plasma cells
  • Diagnosis of Plasma cell myeloma or Multiple Myeloma

Inclusion bodies in plasma cells:

  • Dutcher bodies- Intranuclear
  • Russell bodies- Intracytoplasmic


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: True about Bence-Jones protein are all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Reappears at 100 degrees C
  • Bence-Jones proteins are made of a light chain, dissolve at 100°C and lead to an Amyloid light chain in urine.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male has a pathologic fracture of the femur. The lesion appears lytic on X-ray film with a circumscribed punched-out appearance. The curetting from the fracture site is most likely to show which of the following:

options.label: A
options.text: Diminished and thinned trabecular bone fragments secondary to osteopenia

questions.solutionHtml:
Sheets of atypical plasma cells
  • The single punched lesion from the femur in an old age person is most likely suggestive of plasma cell neoplasm, so the curettage or biopsy from this area will show sheets of atypical plasma cells.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true-

options.label: A
options.text: Patients with IgD myeloma may present with no evident M-spike on serum electrophoresis

options.label: B
options.text: A diagnosis of plasma cell leukaemia can be made if circulating peripheral blood plasma blasts comprise 14% of peripheral blood white cell count of 1 X 10^9 / L and platelet count of 88 X 10^9/ L

options.label: C
options.text: In smouldering myeloma plasma cells constitute 10 - 30% of total bone marrow cellularity

options.label: D
options.text: In a patient with multiple myeloma, monoclonal light chains may be detected in both serum and urine

questions.answerText: A diagnosis of plasma cell leukaemia can be made if circulating peripheral blood plasma blasts comprise 14% of peripheral blood white cell count of 1 X 10^9 / L and platelet count of 88 X 10^9/ L
questions.solutionHtml:
A diagnosis of plasma cell leukaemia can be made if circulating peripheral blood plasma blasts comprise 14% of peripheral blood white cell count of 1 X 10^9 / L and platelet count of 88 X 10^9/ L
  • False as a diagnosis of plasma cell leukaemia can be made if circulating peripheral blood plasma blasts comprise >20% and not 14% of peripheral blood white cell count.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: Not a feature of multiple myeloma:
questions.solutionHtml:
Elevated alkaline phosphatase
  • Alkaline Phosphatase levels in multiple myeloma are normal and not raised, as there is no bone formation and only bone lysis.
  • Serum alkaline phosphatase is usually normal even with extensive bone involvement because of the absence of osteoblastic activity.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 797

questions.stem: Hyperviscosity is seen in all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryoglobulinemia
  • Hyperviscosity is seen in - Multiple myeloma, MGUS, Lymphoma & Macroglobulinemia


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 610, 611

questions.stem: The cell mass in multiple myeloma is formed by

options.label: A
options.text: Clonal expansion of terminally matured B cells

options.label: B
options.text: Preformed B cells are seen in the marrow

options.label: C
options.text: Circulating B cells settle in BM

options.label: D
options.text: B-cells turn malignant and secrete light chains

questions.answerText: B-cells turn malignant and secrete light chains
questions.solutionHtml:
B-cells turn malignant and secrete light chains
  • The cell mass in multiple myeloma is formed by B-cells or Plasma cells, that turn malignant and secrete light chains.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 607-610

questions.stem: Not true regarding Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia is -
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypercalcemia
  • In Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia, lymphadenopathy is usually present, blood viscosity is increased, and IgM immunoglobulin is increased. Hyperviscosity is seen, but hypercalcemia is usually not seen.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 20th Edition, Page No. 802
